title: invariant vs requires
concept: Understanding when to use type invariants vs function requires: invariants for permanent type properties, requires for per-call conditions.
why: Choosing the wrong one leads to over-constrained types or under-protected functions. The right choice makes your API both safe and flexible.
tips: Ask: 'Is this always true for the type?' → invariant. 'Only for this call?' → requires
Invariants reduce code duplication — check once, trust everywhere
requires is more flexible — different functions on the same type can have different preconditions
Use both for layered safety: invariant guards the type, requires guards the function
common_mistakes: Putting per-call conditions in invariants — over-constrains the type
Putting permanent truths in requires — forces every caller to check
Adding invariants that duplicate what the type system already guarantees (e.g., &T is non-null)
